rationale: M60 XML deep review, findings G1 and D2. A processing instruction WITH CONTENT did not parse at all before the grammar repair: `common/scanner.h`'s `advance_if_eq` is `if (!eof && lookahead==chr) advance(); else return false`, so the trailing `advance_if_eq(lexer,'\n')` inside `scan_pi_content` — pure lookahead, already past `mark_end` — aborted the whole `_pi_content` token whenever the byte after `?>` was not a newline. `<?catalog-processing build="12"?>` became an ERROR node, and with no XMLDecl present the enclosing `prolog` disappeared too. The shipped M12 contract check for PI extraction used `<?catalog-processing?>` — the ONE spelling the broken grammar handled — so the lane read green while its most common construct was unparseable; that is why this fixture exists and why coverage has to be measured on the construct rather than its nearest neighbour. The `xml-stylesheet` and `xml-model` PIs are the grammar's own external-token node types, so the `PI` branch never sees them, and their `href` is a FILE reference between two files in a project. Lines are read off the file: the PI 2, the stylesheet 3, the nested PI 5.

forbidRelationships.note: `title="Catalog"` is a pseudo-ATTRIBUTE VALUE, not a path; only href is a file reference
`type="text/xsl"` is the stylesheet's media type, not a path

forbidSymbols.name: xml
forbidSymbols.note: `xml` is reserved: the grammar makes it an XMLDecl, and a PI target that lower-cases to it is a declaration, not an instruction

forbidSymbols.name: xml-model
forbidSymbols.note: this fixture has no xml-model PI; pinned in the m12 contract probe instead
